claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC, dendritic material.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The unmodified TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding 0.5–2 wt% fine Y2O3 during mechanical alloying can produce a uniform nanoscale oxide dispersion within grains and along grain boundaries.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can be used to synthesize and consolidate a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Hot isostatic pressing below the TiVNbTa solidus is an effective alternative consolidation route for the proposed Y2O3-containing alloy.
Stable Y2O3 dispersoids obstruct dislocation motion.
Y2O3 dispersoids impede grain-boundary sliding at 1273 K.
Y2O3 dispersoids retard microstructural coarsening and preserve a refined grain size during thermal exposure.
Particle precipitation or dispersion strengthening can contribute to the mechanical strength of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed Y2O3 dispersion will produce a significantly higher TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K than the 330 MPa baseline.
The modified alloy may approach the strengths observed for unmodified TiVNbTa at lower temperatures.
The strengthening improvement is applicable from room temperature through 1273 K under approximately 30% compressive strain.
A stable, non-agglomerated Y2O3 dispersion is required for the proposed strengthening effect.
Nanoparticle agglomeration can create structural deficiencies in the modified alloy.
A Y2O3-modified specimen and an identically processed Y2O3-free control should be compared at 1273 K under compressive loading to approximately 30% strain.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant yield-strength increase over approximately 330 MPa is designated as a falsifying outcome.
